kind: metric claim check on the entry's own implementation; NOT a leaderboard score

claim_1_uniform_rescaling_is_monotone.statement: DTI strictly increases under p -> lambda*p
claim_1_uniform_rescaling_is_monotone.verdict: TRUE - and it is the only identity the algebra supports

claim_2_hardening_always_helps.statement: writing 1.0 instead of the probability must raise the score

counterexample.layout: one GT pixel at (2,2) predicted 1.0; one remote pixel at (9,9) at 0.01

claim_2_hardening_always_helps.verdict: FALSE as stated: hardening a remote false positive raises FP_w and can lower DTI. The published sentence overgeneralises claim 1.

consequence_for_the_entry_docs: The live 6GEMSDOE methodology note and EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md still present claim 2 as a consequence of claim 1. The correct statement is: a uniform rescaling never costs score; hardening helps when the raised pixels are near truth and hurts when they are not, so the 3% budget - not the binarisation - is what the measurement supports.
